senses.sense_definition: The highest point, peak, or culmination in the development of something, such as a career or life.

examples.text: Winning the prestigious international award marked the <w>apotheosis</w> of her long scientific career.
Many film critics consider this magnificent symphony to be the <w>apotheosis</w> of romantic music.

senses.sense_definition: A quintessential, idealized, or glorified example of a particular quality or concept.

examples.text: The luxurious mansion was widely regarded as the <w>apotheosis</w> of modern architectural design.
In his latest novel, the villain represents the dark <w>apotheosis</w> of greed and ambition.

senses.sense_definition: The elevation of a human being to the rank of a god; deification.

examples.text: In ancient Rome, the official <w>apotheosis</w> of an emperor usually occurred only after his death.
Greek mythology describes the dramatic <w>apotheosis</w> of Hercules after he completed his heroic trials.

senses.sense_definition: Extreme exaltation or glorification, treating someone or something with extraordinary reverence or status.

examples.text: The media frenzy contributed to the sudden <w>apotheosis</w> of the young pop singer into an untouchable cultural icon.
The late twentieth century witnessed the gradual <w>apotheosis</w> of digital technology in daily life.

senses.sense_definition: Release from earthly life and ascension to heaven; death viewed as spiritual elevation.

examples.text: The poet described the dying soldier's final breath as a peaceful and triumphant <w>apotheosis</w>.
In the epic verse, the hero achieves his glorious <w>apotheosis</w> amid the stormy ocean.
